identity.title: Radio Continuum Observations of the Galactic Center: Photoevaporative Proplyd-like Objects Near Sgr A*

paper_type_evidence.quote: We also present an SiO (5-4) spectrum derived from Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) observations carried out by the Science Verification team.

evidence.quote: Our 34 GHz observations reveal partially resolved sources with typical sizes of a few hundred AU at the 8 kpc distance to the Galactic center.
Our 34 GHz observations reveal partially resolved sources with typical sizes of a few hundred AU at the 8 kpc distance to the Galactic center.

distance_source.value: assumed distance to the Galactic center (no citation given)

evidence.quote: Our 34 GHz observations reveal partially resolved sources with typical sizes of a few hundred AU at the 8 kpc distance to the Galactic center.

question.value: Are there photoevaporative proplyd-like objects (low-mass star formation) near Sgr A*, as seen in 34 GHz VLA continuum plus a supporting ALMA SiO spectrum?

evidence.quote: We interpret these sources as a candidate population of photoevaporative protoplanetary disks (proplyds) that are associated with newly formed low mass stars
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00005.SV.
We searched for additional SiO emission from the data published earlier (Yusef-Zadeh et al. 2013) and found a weak SiO source 12 toward the cluster of proplyds.

provided.value: 34.5 GHz A-configuration continuum imaging, 7.8 uJy rms, ~88x46 mas

evidence.quote: Radio continuum observations were carried out with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA)[^1] in its A-configuration at 34.5 GHz on March 9, 2014 (14A-232).

provided.value: 3.8 micron L'-band images for near-IR counterpart limits

evidence.quote: L$'$-band (3.8 $\mu$m) data were taken with the Nasmyth Adaptive Optics System (NACO) at the Very Large Telescope (VLT; program 089.B-0503(B))

what.value: Lyman continuum ionizing photon rate of massive stars, 2.5e50 s^-1

evidence.quote: The EUV Lyman continuum ionization radiation from massive stars is estimated to be $\Phi\approx 2.5\times10^{50}$ s$^{-1}$ (Genzel, Hollenbach & Townes 1994)

what.value: Details of the ALMA SiO observations and reduction

evidence.quote: Details of these observations are given in Yusef-Zadeh et al. (2013).

what.value: NACO image reduction by speckle holography

evidence.quote: The images were reduced with the speckle holography method, as described in detail in Schödel et al. (2010, 2013).

method.value: Gaussian fits give positions, sizes, peak and integrated fluxes (Table 1)

evidence.quote: The Parameters of Gaussian Fitted 34 GHz Sources

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate ionized mass, density and mass-loss rate

method.value: Spherical source of 500 AU radius, filling factor 1; expansion at the sound speed gives the mass-loss rate

evidence.quote: Assuming a spherical source with solid angle corresponding to a radius of 500 AU and electron density filling the sphere with volume filling factor of 1
Assuming that the ionized gas expands at the sound speed ($c_s\approx 10$ km s$^{-1}$ for $T=8\,000$ K)

analysis_steps.goal: Fit SiO (5-4) spectrum of new source 12

method.value: Gaussian fit to the ALMA spectrum

evidence.quote: A Gaussian fit to this spectrum gives peak flux density 13.69$\pm$1.81 mJy beam$^{-1}$
We report 44 partially resolved compact sources clustered in two regions in the E arm of ionized gas that orbits Sgr A\*.
the 1$\sigma$ rms sensitivity is 7.8 $\mu$Jy
A Gaussian fit to this spectrum gives peak flux density 13.69$\pm$1.81 mJy beam$^{-1}$

findings_qualitative.value: SiO (5-4) sources 4, 5 and 12 coincide with the proplyd candidate concentration; their linewidths are similar to low-mass protostellar outflows

evidence.quote: We note that the SiO (5-4) sources 4, 5 and 12 coincide with the concentration of proplyds candidates.

claims.hypothesis: The compact 34 GHz sources are photoevaporating disks around low-mass stars near Sgr A*
claims.experiment: 34 GHz VLA imaging, NACO 3.8 um limits, SiO from ALMA
claims.result: 44 bow-shock sources facing Sgr A*, no near-IR counterparts, SiO sources coincident
claims.finding: They are a proplyd candidate population, implying in-situ low-mass star formation

evidence.quote: The presence of proplyds implies current in-situ star formation activity near Sgr A\*

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: An isolated molecular globule as the mass reservoir is deemed improbable, since a dense, massive globule would collapse

evidence.quote: As such a dense and massive globule would collapse and form a YSO, it is therefore much more plausible that the reservoir of neutral material is instead a circumstellar disk

limitations_admitted.value: Near-IR stellar counterparts cannot be identified with certainty, owing to the lack of proper motion data and confusion

evidence.quote: We can not find near-IR stellar counterparts to radio sources listed in Table 1 with certainty because of the lack of stellar proper motion data and confusing sources in this region.

referee_caveats_inferred: Bow-shock morphology could also come from other sources, e.g. a nuclear wind
No spectral index or disk mass measurements
Interpretation as proplyds is based on analogy

missing_for_reproduction: ALMA observing and processing details, which are only given in Yusef-Zadeh et al. 2013
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~50-200 GB (VLA 8 GHz A-config plus ALMA SV)
